summary_oneline: S-4: give CLI-run agents and stdio MCP toolkit servers a Navigator-keyed principal and server-brokered access to FEAT-773 connections, generalizing the FEAT-696 CLI 3LO flow.

single point where CLI identity (permission_context, user_id) enters bot.ask / ask_stream

slash-command registry (home for a CLI /connect <provider>) and suspend() for foreign prompts (device code)

JSON-RPC stdio dispatch; tools/call carries no principal
tool name + arguments → adapter.execute(arguments); nothing identity-related is threaded
.parrot/mcp-toolkits.yaml model; `env` is the only secret channel into a stdio server process
writes Claude Code .mcp.json / Codex .codex/config.toml entries (command + env) — the channel for binding identity into the server process at start

constraints.statement: Stdio toolkit servers must stay lean: never import ai-parrot-server, aiohttp-server or navconfig; stdout is the JSON-RPC channel, so every prompt or log goes to stderr
constraints.implication: a remote CredentialStore for stdio servers must be an aiohttp-client-only module in parrot core, imported under the existing stderr redirect; connect prompts must be returned as an AuthRequiredPayload tool result or written to stderr, never printed like the O365 prompt_callback

constraints.statement: No principal arrives on an MCP tools/call from Claude Code or Codex; the only inputs are tool name and arguments
constraints.implication: a stdio server's principal must be bound at process start — from env written by hosts.py entries or from a local login file the process reads — mirroring agentd's connection-time binding

constraints.statement: S-1 fixes the contracts: Principal(user_id=Navigator id, channel in {web,telegram,slack,msteams,a2a,cli}), AuthRequiredPayload with user_code/verification_uri/expires_in, OAuth2ProviderDescriptor without a device-authorization endpoint
constraints.implication: S-4 adds a CLI PrincipalResolver and, if generic device code is wanted, a descriptor field — never a parallel principal model

constraints.statement: Every CredentialResolverFactory kind requires an in-process oauth_manager or VaultTokenSync; CLI, parrot.mcp and agentd never build a CredentialBroker, and stdio servers never run AbstractBot.configure()
constraints.implication: out-of-process consumers need a new resolver/store that reaches the server API instead of Redis/Identity Vault; the ToolManager _broker/_cred_user_id seam itself is reused, not re-implemented

constraints.statement: The Navigator user_id is produced server-side from a bearer (principal_guard.resolve_principal) or a session (resolve_user_id); the CLI's only server-authenticated identity is the hand-supplied --token / PARROT_SERVER_TOKEN bearer, and no parrot login command exists
constraints.implication: the CLI principal must come from a server round-trip over a login token; mapping an Entra OID or OS user locally cannot yield the Navigator id

constraints.statement: A CLI 3LO precedent exists (FEAT-696 parrot jiratoolkit auth): manual paste of the redirected URL with CSRF state, local file token store, consumed by JiraToolkit under the fixed identity local:cli; it imports parrot.auth.jira_oauth helpers that S-1 M7 rewrites
constraints.implication: S-4 generalizes this flow to any descriptor provider and keys it by principal; the Jira helpers it imports must be re-verified after FEAT-773 merges

constraints.statement: agentd binds an OS-username principal per UDS connection (SO_PEERCRED, service-identity fallback) and forwards it on every RPC; build_principal_context defaults tenant_id to the principal
constraints.implication: agentd callers need an OS-user → Navigator mapping or a login token in the envelope; a CLI resolver must pass the real tenant explicitly

constraints.statement: Device code is O365-only (wraps O365Client.interactive_login); there is no RFC 8628 engine and MCPOAuth2Config has no device grant
constraints.implication: generic device code is new work; the browser/paste flow is the baseline for every provider

constraints.statement: The local-MCP surface is in flight (hotfix b80ea3a98 on 2026-10-28) and the tools/manager.py seam lines cited by TASK-1685 date from 2026-05
constraints.implication: S-4 edit sites on local_cli.py / local_server.py / tools/manager.py must be re-anchored at spec time

constraints.statement: MCP client-side token stores (mcp:oauth:{server}:{user}, mcp_oauth_*) and MCPOAuth2Provider are the parrot-as-client direction and a third key family S-1 leaves alone
constraints.implication: S-4 scopes them out explicitly (non-goal) so 'MCP' in S-4 means parrot tools consumed by an external host

constraints.statement: A navigator-auth-authenticated server endpoint yields the Navigator user_id (session userdata / resolve_user_id); an external-introspection mount yields the IdP sub
constraints.implication: the CLI identity/token endpoint must sit behind navigator-auth session or bearer auth, not behind the OAUTH2_EXTERNAL MCP mount

new: CLI login state: `parrot login` / `parrot logout` (or reuse of --token / PARROT_SERVER_TOKEN) storing a navigator-auth bearer in a 0600 local file — the CLI's principal source (U1)

`CliPrincipalResolver` implementing S-1 `PrincipalResolver`: resolves the Navigator user_id and tenant by presenting the login token to the server (same path as principal_guard.resolve_principal) and builds Principal(channel='cli') → build_principal_context → REPLConfig.permission_context

Remote credential access for out-of-process consumers: an aiohttp-client-only `CredentialResolver` / `CredentialStore` in parrot core that reads a provider access token from a new server endpoint under /api/v1/connections (PBAC-guarded, short-lived access token only; refresh stays server-side) (U2)

Principal binding for stdio toolkit servers: create_toolkit_mcp_server accepts a principal + credential resolver resolved at process start from the login file / env; credentialed tools return AuthRequiredPayload as the tool result for the host to show

Connect from the CLI: `parrot connect <provider>` command and `/connect <provider>` slash command → start_connect(channel='cli') via the server API, print/open the authorize URL, complete by polling GET /api/v1/connections or by pasting the redirected URL (FEAT-696 style) (U3)
Optional: generic RFC 8628 device-code engine with a `device_authorization_url` descriptor field, surfaced through the existing AuthRequiredPayload device fields (U4)
Optional: agentd OS-user → Navigator principal mapping (per-user login file or token in the JSON-RPC envelope) (U5)

unknowns.question: How does a CLI user obtain the login token that yields the Navigator user_id?
plausible_answers: a) new `parrot login` that completes a navigator-auth browser/device login and stores a CLI token in a 0600 file
b) reuse an existing bearer / API key: `--token` / PARROT_SERVER_TOKEN persisted by `parrot login --token`
c) no login: admin-managed OS-user → Navigator mapping (agentd style)
unknowns.user_answer: parrot login (browser/device): a new `parrot login` completes a navigator-auth browser or device login and stores a CLI token in a 0600 file under ~/.parrot/; `parrot logout` removes it.

unknowns.question: How do stdio MCP toolkit servers running inside Claude Code / Codex get provider tokens?
plausible_answers: a) server-vended short-lived access token via a new PBAC-guarded endpoint under /api/v1/connections (refresh stays on the server)
b) local encrypted token file written by `parrot connect` (FEAT-696 style, offline, no server dependency at call time)
c) stdio servers get no 3LO; credentialed toolkits go through the HTTP MCP server with principal_guard
unknowns.user_answer: Local encrypted token file — as an encrypted cache synced from the server: the server completes the 3LO and the Identity Vault stays the durable owner; `parrot connect` pulls the token set into a local encrypted file (key derived from the login token); refresh goes through the server when expired.

unknowns.question: How does a CLI connect complete?
plausible_answers: a) print/open the authorize URL and poll GET /api/v1/connections until the connection appears
b) manual paste of the redirected URL posted to the server (works over SSH, no redirect-URI issue)
unknowns.user_answer: Poll + paste fallback: print/open the authorize URL and poll GET /api/v1/connections until the connection appears; when the browser cannot reach back (SSH), paste the redirected URL and the CLI posts the code to the server.

unknowns.question: Should S-4 add a generic RFC 8628 device-code engine (descriptor `device_authorization_url`) or keep device code O365-only?
plausible_answers: a) generic engine in S-4 for providers that support it (Microsoft, Google)
b) keep O365-only; browser/paste flow is the baseline
c) defer to a later spec
unknowns.user_answer: Generic engine in S-4: add `device_authorization_url` to the S-1 descriptor and an RFC 8628 poller surfaced through the AuthRequiredPayload device fields (Microsoft, Google).

unknowns.question: Is agentd (OS-user → Navigator principal) in S-4 scope?
plausible_answers: a) yes: per-OS-user login file read by the daemon
b) yes: login token carried in the JSON-RPC envelope
c) no: agentd keeps the OS/service identity; defer
unknowns.user_answer: Yes — per-OS-user login file: the daemon resolves the peer's OS user (SO_PEERCRED) and reads that user's ~/.parrot login file to obtain the Navigator principal.
